clue.text: Stir and sip mixed drinks

indicators.note: mixed tells us to shuffle the letters of stir and sip together into a new order

explanation.surface: A bartender's instruction for preparing a cocktail: stir it, taste it, serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are strong distilled alcoholic drinks such as gin, vodka and whisky.

clue.text: Dog had been bitten by pig

indicators.note: been bitten by puts the word had between the jaws of the pig

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A dog that has been attacked and bitten by a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, which is also to tail them like a detective.

clue.text: Fires one head over heels

indicators.note: head over heels sends the first letter tumbling to the end of the word

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: Someone sacked who tumbles over with surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE has its head, S, moved to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingle is an old word for a hearth fire, as in inglenook, the fireside corner.

clue.text: Inability to grasp a pound? Conservative cuts tragic reality

parts.note: a is one, written as the Roman numeral I
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: cuts tells us the Conservative letter slices into the rearranged letters
tragic suggests something ruinous, so the letters of reality are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the Conservatives, cutting budgets, cannot understand money in the tragic reality of austerity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pound' gives I L (one pound); 'tragic' rearranges REALITY into LITERAY, and 'cuts' puts C into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiteracy is the lack of the ability to read or understand writing, and more broadly ignorance.

clue.text: Leader of Kremlin admits mistake turning secret agent

indicators.note: turning tells us the whole run of letters is read backwards
Leader of picks out the first letter of Kremlin

parts.note: oops is what one says after a mistake

explanation.surface: The Russian leader confesses a blunder and an agent is turned to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: K and OOPS together, read back to front, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is slang for a spy, especially one working for an intelligence agency.

clue.text: Penny's husband breaks a ton on motorway with Rolls-Royce

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny

indicators.note: breaks tells us the letters of a ton are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: M is a motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A woman's husband is speeding at over a hundred on the motorway in his luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' looks like the husband breaking a speed record, but it scrambles A TON into ANTO. 'A ton' is British slang for 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phantom is a famous model of luxury car built by Rolls-Royce, so the make stands for the model.

clue.text: Palin's touring production, which involves no embroidery

indicators.note: touring suggests the letters of Palin travel around into a new order

parts.note: Michael Palin's name supplies its letters, the possessive adding none
a work is a production, such as a stage piece or a book

explanation.surface: Michael Palin, the comedian and travel presenter, making a straightforward travel show.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Palin is a British comic and travel broadcaster, so 'touring' fits him. It rearranges PALIN into PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainwork is ordinary needlework such as hemming and seaming, as opposed to decorative fancy stitching.

clue.text: Retailer loses small ship

indicators.note: loses tells us a letter is taken away from the shop name

parts.note: Argos is a British catalogue retailer

explanation.surface: A shop that loses a little ship from its stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos is a well-known British high-street catalogue shop.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the vessel in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Edward wraps square present, tied with strong string?

indicators.note: wraps tells us the name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
a T is a T-square, a drawing tool for right angles
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Edward wrapping a square parcel and tying it up with strong string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but it is the opposite of absent. The question mark flags that strong string is loose for a rope or tether.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up with a rope or line, the strong string of the definition.

clue.text: Soldier is holding iron bar out in the open

parts.note: a man is a soldier, as in officers and men

indicators.note: holding tells us the word is wraps around the iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
T is a T-bar

explanation.surface: A soldier carrying an iron bar out in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plainly visible or obvious, clear for everyone to see.

clue.text: Perhaps Michael Vaughan's foot follows a leg break

indicators.note: follows places the last letter of Vaughan after the a
the foot of a word is its final letter, here of Vaughan
break tells us to shatter the letters of leg into a new order

explanation.surface: Michael Vaughan, the former England cricket captain, has his foot follow through on a leg break delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Vaughan captained England at cricket and a leg break is a spin delivery, so the surface is all cricket; the definition wants the archangel instead. 'break' rearranges the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is one of the archangels, so he is an example of a heavenly messenger, hence the Perhaps.

clue.text: Before a nut develops, lots of fruit, which may hang from trees

indicators.note: Before tells us the shortened fruit comes ahead of the rearranged letters
lots of means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: develops signals that the letters of a nut change into a new form

explanation.surface: An orchard scene: before the nuts ripen there is a heavy crop of fruit hanging from the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges the nut letters and 'lots of' drops the fruit's final letter; 'Before' tells us the fruit comes first despite the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: This great ape of Borneo and Sumatra lives in the forest canopy and often dangles from branches by its long arms.

clue.text: Passing old, green, family silver around

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

indicators.note: around tells us the silver wraps round the family

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: An elderly person handing down the family silver, perhaps on death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like death, but it is the motorist's sense; vert is heraldry's green. 'around' has the silver enclose the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing another vehicle on the road is going past it from behind, which is this manoeuvre.

clue.text: Oblivious to four notes?

parts.note: D is a musical note
E is a musical note
A is a musical note
F is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone tone-deaf who cannot hear four notes played to them.
explanation.walkthrough: Many words can be spelt from the note names A to G; the definition picks out which.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deaf to something is an idiom for refusing to hear it or ignoring it entirely.

clue.text: Old photographs and toys prefer recycling

indicators.note: recycling suggests the letters of toys and prefer are reprocessed into a new order

explanation.surface: A comment on children who would rather recycle old snapshots and toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrotypes, or tintypes, were nineteenth-century photographs made directly on thin iron plates.

clue.text: Blowing air: most reed instruments

indicators.note: Blowing suggests the letters of air, most and reed are scattered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A musician's remark that most reed instruments need air blown through them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reed instruments' looks like woodwind, but 'instruments' alone is the definition and 'reed' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiometers are scientific devices that measure radiant energy, so they are measuring instruments.

clue.text: One dapper in fancy style of trouser?

indicators.note: fancy tells us the letters are rearranged in a decorative way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dapper man in a fancy outfit, wearing a particular cut of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the style, but it rearranges I with DAPPER and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipes are very narrow tight trousers, popular with 1950s Teddy boys.

clue.text: US crimes: very loud, seen abroad, wearing XXXL?

indicators.note: wearing tells us the other letters go inside the outsize garment

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing size XXXL
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: abroad signals that the letters of seen wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An outsize American, very loud and noticed abroad, commits misdemeanours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges SEEN; 'US' says the spelling is American, with an S in place of the British C.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenses is the American spelling of offences, breaches of the law.

clue.text: Company submits reports

indicators.note: reports signals that the word is heard as spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: presents means submits, as one hands in work

explanation.surface: A firm that hands in its accounts to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a firm, but it means being with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping someone company means being with them, so the word means attendance or being in someone's midst.

clue.text: Banger car, with wrecked interior, crashed into tree

indicators.note: into tells us the rearranged letters go inside the tree

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: crashed signals that the letters are smashed up and rearranged
interior means the inside letters of wrecked, without its ends

explanation.surface: An old wreck of a car, its insides gutted, has smashed into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' is British slang for a rundown car, which the surface uses, and also for a firework or sausage. 'crashed' scrambles the pieces and 'into' puts them inside the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a banger is a loud exploding firework, the kind set off on Bonfire Night.

clue.text: Author becomes cleaner with HR trade

indicators.note: with HR trade tells us an H is traded in exchange for an R

parts.note: whiter means cleaner, as in washing

explanation.surface: A writer who takes a job in human resources after cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: HR looks like human resources, but it is the letters H and R; one H in WHITER is traded for R.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is someone who writes books, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Town where the meat's off?

parts.note: food that is off is past its best, or old
ham is a meat; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A town where the meat has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldham is a town in Greater Manchester; the meat is ham and 'off' means old.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a former mill town in north-west England, near Manchester.

clue.text: In France a syllable is unforced

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters across France a syllable

explanation.surface: A remark about French pronunciation, where syllables are spoken without strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' looks like it calls for a French word, but the answer simply sits in the letters of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unforced comes naturally, without effort or strain, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps Berkeley's after a Liberal from one side

parts.note: the University of California at Berkeley is an example of a uni
later means after, in time

explanation.surface: A political commentary on the philosopher Berkeley chasing a Liberal from one side.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkeley could be the philosopher, but here it is the Californian university; the 's is short for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A unilateral action is taken by one party or side alone, without the others agreeing.

clue.text: Luminously eyed Madagascan, usually ringed at the extremities

definitions.text: Luminously eyed Madagascan, usually ringed at the extremities

indicators.note: at the extremities points to the leading tip of each of the five words, so their initials are taken

explanation.surface: A wildlife description of a big-eyed Madagascan animal with a ringed tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the initials spell the animal, and the clue describes the ring-tailed kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found only on Madagascar; the ring-tailed species has large glowing eyes and a banded tail.

clue.text: It's buoyant, oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of buoyant

explanation.surface: A remark that something floats, surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'buoyant' give the answer, and the whole clue describes it, though 'oddly' adds nothing to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that floats on water is by nature buoyant, which is the defining property of a craft.

clue.text: Solving uses minor part of the brain

indicators.note: Solving suggests working through and rearranging the letters of uses minor

explanation.surface: A claim that doing puzzles only uses a small part of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The sensorium is the seat of sensation in the brain, the area that receives and interprets sense data.

clue.text: Level playing field

definitions.meaning: a level or degree, as in reaching a fever height of excitement
a sports ground, such as a football or cricket ground

explanation.surface: The idiom a level playing field, meaning fair conditions for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a degree or intensity and a ground where field sports are played.

clue.text: Fleming's criminal organisation has secret design to seize power

indicators.note: to seize tells us the rearranged letters take hold of the letter for power
design signals that the letters of secret are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A villainous organisation from a Bond novel plotting secretly to seize world power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' scrambles SECRET, which then grabs P.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ian Fleming's James Bond novels, the global crime syndicate headed by Blofeld is named by this acronym.

clue.text: Storm brews over ball game's lofty stage

indicators.note: over tells us the rearranged letters cover the ball game
brews means the letters of storm are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a ball game

explanation.surface: A storm gathering over a rugby ground's raised viewing stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brews' rearranges the storm, and 'over' places it around rugby union's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform from which a speaker addresses an audience or a conductor leads.
